correctness.rationale: For every real norm-one strongly exposed point supported on a finite maximal antichain alpha, each branch intersects alpha exactly once and norm-one mass one at alpha kills all off-antichain coordinates. For y in the strict f_alpha slice, epsilon_s=1-sign(x_s)y_s >=0 and sum epsilon_s<N delta. Every chain extended to a branch through s contributes ||y-x|| at most |1-a|+1-|a| <=2 epsilon_s, uniformly <=2 max epsilon_s <2N delta; the diameter also bounds by 2. Moving epsilon<min(1,N delta) from one antichain s to a strict descendant gives a unit-ball vector with f_alpha=1-epsilon/N and ||y-x||=2 epsilon. Limit epsilon->min(1,N delta) proves the sharp supremum including the strict-slice transition delta=1/N. No finite experiment substitutes for the analytic proof.
residual_risks: Uses the exact binary-tree chain norm and finite maximal antichains; cannot infer the formula for other norms, exposing functionals or countably branching variants.
